vulnerabilities.explanation: The health check logic is inverted. It returns true only when answer == 0 (sequencer down) AND grace period has passed since last update. This means borrow/liquidation operations are allowed when the sequencer is DOWN for longer than grace period, instead of being blocked. The correct logic should check if sequencer is UP (answer == 1) and grace period has passed since it came back up.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Sequencer goes down (answer = 0). 2. Wait for grace period to pass. 3. Now isBorrowAllowed() and isLiquidationAllowed() return true, allowing users to borrow when oracle is down or liquidate positions with stale prices. 4. Attacker can borrow at incorrect prices or liquidate healthy positions.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Change the condition to: answer == 1 && block.timestamp - lastUpdateTimestamp > _gracePeriod. Also add validation for stale data (lastUpdateTimestamp > 0) and handle negative answers.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract has a critical logic flaw in the oracle health check. Borrowing and liquidation are incorrectly allowed when the sequencer is down, exposing the protocol to price manipulation attacks. The admin functions are properly protected, and no other vulnerabilities were found. The fix requires inverting the health check logic and adding proper data validation.
